steps.title: A query is a string
steps.notes:
A string that starts with --sql is a query. sqlty reads schema.sql and types each column of its result: open Types.

Problems already says the query is not wrapped in SQL[T]. Step 4 does that.
steps.source: users = "--sql\nSELECT id, name, email FROM users"

steps.title: Types follow the SQL
steps.notes:
SUM of NUMERIC is a Decimal. count is an int and never NULL. The LEFT JOIN makes every column of orders nullable, so MAX(o.placed_at) can be None.

Each type names the rule that made it, with a link to the database's manual.
steps.source:
users = "--sql\nSELECT id, name, email FROM users"

spent = """--sql
SELECT u.name, count(o.id) AS orders, SUM(o.total) AS spent, MAX(o.placed_at) AS last_order
FROM users AS u
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.name"""

steps.title: Mistakes, before they run
steps.notes: A typo in a column, and a row type that no longer matches its query. Click a problem to go to its line; Ctrl+. on it, or Fix all, applies the fix.
steps.source:
from sqlty import SQL

users = SQL[tuple[int, str]]("--sql\nSELECT id, email FROM users")

typo = "--sql\nSELECT nme FROM users"

steps.title: Rewrite: the row type in the code
steps.notes: sqlty rewrite wraps each query in SQL[T], its row type, so a type checker sees what each row holds. Press Rewrite to apply it, and Strip to take it back.
steps.source:
users = "--sql\nSELECT id, name, email FROM users"

spent = """--sql
SELECT u.name, SUM(o.total) AS spent
FROM users AS u
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.name"""

steps.title: Parameters have types too
steps.notes: With param-types = true, a parameter is typed by what it is compared with: Types lists them. Press Rewrite, and it writes a TypedDict for the named ones.
steps.source:
since = """--sql
SELECT u.name, o.total
FROM orders AS o
JOIN users AS u ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE o.placed_at > %(since)s AND o.total >= %(least)s"""

steps.title: The schema changes
steps.notes: name becomes nullable, and the code that reads it is now wrong: the row type says str. Edit schema.sql and watch Problems: the migration breaks code it never touched.
steps.source:
from sqlty import SQL

users = SQL[tuple[int, str, str | None]]("--sql\nSELECT id, name, email FROM users")
